Many people have done this, Paul McCartney is a well known example; but I am left handed, and I always have thought I got the best of it by playing the "normal" right handed way.

It's my left hand that is strong and supple; that's the one that plays notes and chords on the neck. My right hand has far less responsibility, even if I am fingerpicking a guitar or similar instrument. And when I play with a pick, like on mandolin, the difference is even more apparent.

In this case, the whole thing has played right into my hands.

Plus, since you're learning the same way 90% of the world learns, "right-handed", you can play almost any instrument you encounter- which is certainly not true if you do the whole reversal-neck-to-the-right thing.

My advice: don't throw away an advantage.
If you are left handed, and you want to learn to play a stringed musical instrument, think twice before reversing the strings and holding the instrument "backwards".

Absolutely! I'm left handed and I play guitar and violin and I feel like I have a HUGE advantage (especially when picking up a new instrument) over right handers because I have so much more dexterity in my fretting hand. Infact I've tried playing left-handed guitar and it just feels awkward and wrong.
